subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should OpenClaw fix reply-session-init conflicts centrally in core session initialization, or keep per-channel retry/coalescing behavior at each inbound surface?
rationale: Both shapes are plausible: current source shows a core throw shared by multiple surfaces, while Telegram, Slack, and WhatsApp already have channel-local retry handling; selecting the permanent owner boundary is a maintainer architecture decision.

options.title: Central core self-heal
options.body: Adopt a bounded core/session-lifecycle recovery so webchat, heartbeat, and future channels inherit one behavior.

options.title: Surface retry parity
options.body: Keep the core throw and require every inbound surface to detect, spool, or retry this transient conflict explicitly.

options.title: Hold for more proof
options.body: Ask for a fresh webchat or heartbeat timing reproduction before choosing between shared recovery and surface retries.

recommendation.title: Central core self-heal
recommendation.body: Adopt a bounded core/session-lifecycle recovery so webchat, heartbeat, and future channels inherit one behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent guarded reply-session initialization work is the central owner boundary implicated by this decision.
